conventions.convention: Rounds start at 1; the complete-history filtration starts at 0 with trivial initial sigma-algebra. Rewards are fixed or deterministic functions of pre-action history, giving finitely many histories at finite horizon.
All arm probabilities are strictly positive. The estimated loss is the played loss divided by its arm probability, with zero on unplayed arms; the estimated reward is one minus this estimated loss.
Exp3 uses exact real arithmetic, k > 1, n ≥ 1 and η > 0, and assumes a probability space carrying the specified measurable conditional draws.

The regret rate uses η = sqrt(2 log(k)/(nk)). For deterministic past-adaptive rewards, the maximum over fixed arms is outside expectation; no expected in-hindsight maximum or policy-regret guarantee is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Before the action, rewards and strictly positive sampling probabilities are measurable with respect to the finite pre-action history. The loss estimate is indicator{A_t=i}(1-X_t)/P_{t,i}, and the reward estimate is one minus the loss estimate.
In the estimator definition, the conditional mean, second moment and variance of an arm's loss estimate are respectively y, y²/p and y²(1-p)/p.
For every real z ≤ 0, exp(z) ≤ 1 + z + z²/2.

Initialize cumulative estimated rewards at zero, normalize exp(η times cumulative estimated reward), sample an arm, form the importance-weighted loss and corresponding reward estimates, and add the reward estimates to the cumulative estimates.

Exp3 is well-defined and completes its finite horizon for every η > 0 and every admitted reward sequence. At η = sqrt(2 log(k)/(nk)), its stated oblivious and past-adaptive expected fixed-arm regrets are at most sqrt(2nk log(k)).
